sources.title: EV Database - Kia EV6 Standard Range 2WD (2021-2024)
sources.notes: 58.0 kWh nominal, 54.0 kWh usable, NMC, 523 V nominal on 800 V architecture, 175 kW max DC (Kia claims 180 kW, 18 min), 11 kW AC (EU three-phase), CCS rear right. European listing.

sources.title: EV Database - Kia EV6 Long Range AWD (2021-2024)
sources.notes: 77.4 kWh nominal, 74.0 kWh usable, NMC, 697 V, 800 V architecture, 233 kW max DC (Kia claims 240 kW, 18 min), 11 kW AC. European listing.

sources.title: EV Database - Kia EV6 Standard Range 2WD (MY25-27)
sources.notes: 63.0 kWh nominal, 60.0 kWh usable, NMC, 800 V architecture, 195 kW max DC (EU), 11 kW AC. European listing; model years 2025-2027.

sources.title: EV Database - Kia EV6 Long Range 2WD (MY25-27)
sources.notes: 84.0 kWh nominal, 80.0 kWh usable, NMC, 800 V architecture, 263 kW max DC (EU claim), 11 kW AC. European listing; model years 2025-2027.

sources.title: Wikipedia - Kia EV6
sources.notes: Infobox: 58 / 77.4 / 84 kWh packs (84 replaces 77.4 at the 2024 facelift), NCM chemistry, DC 180 kW (58 kWh) and 240 kW (77.4 kWh), 11 kW AC; Georgia-built 2025 cars switch to NACS (port moves to rear driver side).

sources.title: Kia US - 2026 EV6 specifications and trim comparison (charging table)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-19 (page now shows 2026 EV6): Light 63.0 kWh, Light Long Range / Wind / GT-Line 84.0 kWh; onboard charger 10.9 kW on every trim; DC 10-80 % about 20 min at 350 kW (Kia notes the figure comes from a GT AWD test), 24/29 min at 150 kW, 61/81 min at 50 kW; NACS port on all trims.

sources.title: Automoblog - 2025 Kia EV6 overview: fast charging times
sources.notes: Kia-sourced charging chart: max DC input 180 kW (Light), 240 kW (Light Long Range, Wind, GT-Line, GT); 10-80 % at 350 kW 20 min (18 min GT); port on left rear, NACS on all trims except the GT.

sources.title: Electrek - US-built 2025 Kia EV6 debuts with more battery, NACS port
sources.notes: 2025 EV6 has a native NACS port (moved to rear left) on non-GT trims; GT stays Korea-built (production of all other trims moves to Georgia); 63 kWh base and 84 kWh larger pack, each about 7 kWh more than 2024.

sources.title: ArenaEV - Kia EV6 GT 2025 specs
sources.notes: 84 kWh, NCM, 697 V (800 V class), 258 kW peak, CCS port, 11 kW AC.

sources.title: Electrek - Kia EVs can now officially charge on Tesla Superchargers (2025-04-24)
sources.notes: EV6, EV9 and Niro can charge at Tesla Superchargers in North America with the Kia adapter (or a native NACS port); adapter free for 2024/2025 EV9 and 2024 EV6 delivered after 4 Sept 2024, $249 otherwise.

sources.title: Kia Owners (US) - Kia Charge Pass / Kia electrify
sources.notes: "Kia vehicles with CCS charging ports may use Tesla Superchargers by using a Kia approved NACS to CCS adapter"; complimentary adapter for new 2024/2025 EV9 and 2024 EV6 delivered from 4 Sept 2024; Plug and Charge on 2025 EV6, 2026 EV9. Page does not list models by port type.

sources.title: Kia EV6 2024 Owner's Manual (ManualsLib, p.22) - Battery conditioning mode
sources.notes: Relays the 2024 EV6 manual: "Battery conditioning mode" is an item in EV Settings (a menu setting), and you can set a DC charging station as the destination in battery conditioning mode to cut charging time; available on vehicles with a battery heater.

sources.title: Kia UK - What is EV battery pre-conditioning?
sources.notes: Names EV3, EV6 and EV9 among EVs: setting a public charger as destination starts warming/cooling the battery during the drive; can also be started from the infotainment or Kia Connect app with a chosen start time.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Kia EV6 software update improves cold-weather charging
sources.notes: Battery pre-conditioning upgrade is standard on 2023 model-year EV6; 2022 EV6 owners can get it at a dealer. Navigation-triggered (fast charger as destination, pack below 21 C, SoC below 24 %). Kia Europe quote; US availability not stated.

sources.title: Kia US - 2027 EV9 specifications and trim comparison
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-19: Light 76.1 kWh, Light Long Range / Wind AWD / Land AWD / GT-Line AWD 99.8 kWh; onboard charger 10.9 kW on all; DC 10-80 % about 20 min (Light) and 24 min (others) at 350 kW; NACS port on all trims.

sources.title: InsideEVs - 2024 Kia EV9 EPA range and efficiency
sources.notes: Relays Kia documents: 76.1 kWh (Light RWD SR) recharges up to 236 kW, 99.8 kWh up to 215 kW; 10.9 kW onboard charger for both; 10-80 % about 20 min (76.1) and 24-25 min (99.8) on 350 kW / 800 V.

sources.title: Kia owner manual (MV1 = EV9, 2024, en_RG) - Battery conditioning mode
sources.notes: Manual switch on the infotainment screen turns Battery Conditioning on/off; setting a fast charger as waypoint/destination heats or cools the battery while driving; remote start from Kia Connect for about 30 min; only on vehicles with a battery heater.

sources.title: EV Database - Kia e-Niro 64 kWh (2020-2022)
sources.notes: 64.0 kWh usable / 67.5 kWh nominal, NMC622, 360 V nominal, 77 kW max DC, 7.2 kW AC standard (11 kW optional, EU), CCS. European listing.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Test: Kia Niro EV on a 150 kW fast charger
sources.notes: Tested 2019 Niro EV peaked about 77 kW (first session) and 78 kW (second), about 21 C outside; Kia's '80 % in 1 hour @ 100 kW EVSE' is the charger rating, not the car. Averaged about 58 kW from 9-80 % in 54 min.

sources.title: Kia US newsroom - All-new 2019 Kia Niro EV makes North American debut
sources.notes: Page did not load for the fetcher (certificate error); values taken from a search excerpt: 64 kWh lithium-ion polymer battery, 7.2 kW Level 2 charger, CCS standard.

sources.title: EV Database - Kia Niro EV (2022-2025)
sources.notes: 64.8 kWh usable / 68.0 kWh nominal, 358 V, max DC 94 kW (10-80 % 41 min, 70 kW avg), 11 kW AC, CCS; lists preconditioning "yes, including automatic preconditioning when using navigation". Cathode not listed.

sources.title: The Weekly Driver - Kia Niro EV 64.8 kWh battery
sources.notes: CATL NCM cells, 358 V nominal, 64.8 kWh, 2023-2025 Niro EV.

sources.title: InsideEVs - 2023 Kia Niro EV: more EPA range, new style
sources.notes: 64.8 kWh battery, 11 kW onboard charger, 10-80 % in 43 min on an 85 kW charger (Kia figure; the 85 kW is the charger, not a stated car peak).

sources.title: Kia press (Europe) - EV6 software update for faster cold-weather charging
sources.notes: Not opened (redirect to hub); wording taken from a search excerpt: battery conditioning is standard on MY23 EV6, the EV6 GT and the all-new Niro EV, and offered as a retrofit on MY22 EV6.

sources.title: Kia UK - The Kia EV9 specification
sources.notes: 99.8 kWh pack (552 V nominal, 456 cells); 800-volt E-GMP system; 10-80 % in 24 min at 210 kW (needs an 800 V charger delivering at least 210 kW); onboard charger kW not stated. UK page; pack and DC peak do not vary by market.

sources.title: InsideEVs - 2022 Kia EV6 US specs compared
sources.notes: Relays Kia US specs for the 2022 EV6: 10.9 kW onboard charger on both the 58 kWh and 77.4 kWh packs; DC up to 180 kW (58 kWh) and 240 kW (77.4 kWh); 10-80 % under 18 min on an 800 V charger; usable/gross not stated.

sources.title: NHTSA - Kia TSB MC-11027857-0002 (CCS1-to-NACS adapter)
sources.notes: PDF text not readable by the fetcher; per search excerpt the bulletin covers certain 2025-2026MY EV6 and 2026MY EV9 equipped with CCS1 charging ports. Does not name the GT in the excerpt.
